summary: A suggestion for NETBANK, a single billing and account creation system for the network. A project manager would authorize users and set up accounts across many hosts, receiving one combined bill. The manager would go through introductions and funding checks only once.

plainLanguage.summary: Instead of signing up and paying at every shop, you would use one account and get one bill for everything.

questions: how does netbank simplify arpanet access
what problem did netbank aim to solve
subtitle: Single billing and account system for network resource access

tldr.problem: New ARPANET users had to create accounts and arrange billing separately at each server host they wanted to use, creating administrative overhead and friction for project teams.
tldr.mechanism: NETBANK would let a project manager authorize users and set up accounts across all or a subset of server hosts through a single system, receiving one combined bill instead of many.
tldr.outcome: The RFC proposed a centralized service to reduce new-user friction and encourage servers to offer resources knowing the manager had completed authorization and funding checks only once.

today: RFC 408 is classified as Unknown status. It was a conceptual proposal for centralizing ARPANET account management in 1972.

sections.title: The Problem
sections.content: When a project manager wanted to give team members access to computing resources on ARPANET, each person had to go through account creation and funding verification at every host where they might work. This required the manager to perform introductions and provide funding verification repeatedly, creating administrative barriers for both managers and sites.
sections.plainLanguage: Teams had to sign up for accounts at every computer they wanted to use, which was annoying.

sections.title: NETBANK Service Model
sections.content: The RFC proposes NETBANK: a single billing and account creation system where a project manager would be required to go through the initialization process of introducing himself and verifying funding only once. The manager would then authorize a set of user IDs to gain access to and utilize resources across the entire network or a specified subset of server hosts. Users' accounts would create charges to be broken down in a single bill presented to the project manager.
sections.plainLanguage: One manager signs up once, gets money checked once, and then all their team members can use computers everywhere. One bill comes back to the manager.

sections.title: Benefits to the Network
sections.content: NETBANK would encourage server hosts to implement systems that previously seemed viable only at low usage levels, by allowing funded hacking and experimentation by project members in a controlled manner. The system would require an option at login for prospective users to indicate the server should check the NETBANK facility at the system currently hosting it. This approach reduces friction for both users and service providers.
sections.plainLanguage: Schools would be more willing to offer computing time if they knew one person had already approved and funded it.
